drafted_from: tool:send-list-row-batches row (tools/export-records-as-list-rows/tool-rows.json), do-work/send_list_rows.py, read-data/send_batches.py, test/test_send_batches.py and test/fixtures/fake_list_service.py; the answer is what the script printed against that fake service on the made-up bakery batch
start_here: Say to your AI: "Send the prepared bakery orders batches in payloads into my lists with my send config, and tell me how many batches went."
no_lists_because: It keeps no list of its own: the config names the command that writes rows, and it only reads batch files and keeps a status file of what was sent.
instructions: 1. Run tool:export-records-as-list-rows first so a payloads folder holds manifest.json and its batch files such as orders-000.json.

2. Write send-config.json: send (argv of the command that puts rows into a list, input with the texts "$list_id" and "$rows", kept_count the dotted path of the kept ids in its JSON answer), optional warm, retry_if and halve_if error texts, and waits in seconds.
3. Say "Send my batches"; your AI reads the row with tools:list and runs its command with {config}, {batches} and {status}, only when you ask to send.
4. Read state: all_batches_sent (exit 0) or stopped_on_refusal with last_refusal (exit 1); run the same command again to resume, as sent batches are skipped.

worked_examples.title: One batch of two rows is sent after a warm-up
worked_examples.ask: Send my prepared bakery batches into my orders list.
worked_examples.given: Read from a real run of do-work/send_list_rows.py against test/fixtures/fake_list_service.py. The AI runs: python3 -I trillion-workshop/tools/export-records-as-list-rows/do-work/send_list_rows.py --config send-config.json --batches payloads --status status.json. payloads holds orders-000.json with rows O-1 and O-2 and a manifest naming it; send-config.json runs the fake service with put for send and warm for warm, kept_count "kept", waits [0,0,0].
worked_examples.hands_back: {"batches_done": {"orders-000.json": 2}, "state": "all_batches_sent"}, exit 0, and status.json holds the same. The service saw a warm for orders then a put of 2 rows; running it again sends nothing.
